items.label: H.
items.notes: (up to 4 units of Linguistics 191, 192, or 193 may be applied as upper-division Linguistics elective credit toward the major)

requirement.description:
Before beginning the upper-division major, students are advised to consult the department regarding the scheduling of required courses.
44 UD units are required, distributed as follows:

narrative:
MAJOR REGULATIONSPREREQUISITES Check the General Catalog for the prerequisites to all listed courses.
P/NP GRADING OPTION Not allowed for major courses (prep or UD major), including courses applied to the major from other departments.
SUBSTITUTIONS In the major requirements permissible only by petition to the department chair and dean.
G.P.A REQUIREMENTS At least 2.0 overall UC average in all upper-division major courses and all courses (Prep and UD) for the major.
DOUBLE MAJORS With the approval of each department chairperson, up to a total of 8 units may be applied simultaneously to both UD majors.

nodes.title: Introduction to Computer Science
nodes.description: Introduction to computer program development for students with little to no programming experience. Basic programming concepts, variables and expressions, data and control structures, algorithms, debugging, program design, and documentation.

nodes.title: Introduction to Latin American and Iberian Studies
nodes.description: Designed to acquaint students with current research on the main areas of Latin American and Iberian Studies.

nodes.title: Language And Linguistics
nodes.description: Introduction to the scientific study of language: The sounds of language; word and sentence structure; semantics and pragmatics; discourse and conversational speech; the social and cultural functions of language; language change and the reconstruction of languages at earlier stages.

nodes.title: Basic Elements of Linguistic Analysis
nodes.description: An introduction to the analytic methodology in the study of phonology, morphology, syntax, and semantics. A typologically oriented course designed to demonstrate how linguists analyze languages.

nodes.title: Programming for Linguists
nodes.prereq_text: Upper division standing or a prior course in Linguistics.
nodes.description: Hands-on introduction to programming in Python, with emphasis on methods for retrieving, structuring, and interacting with textual data. Focus on developing practical programming skills and transferable methodology, such as debugging, task decomposition and abstraction, and best practices for documenting and structuring code. Targeted toward students with no programming background.

nodes.title: Statistical Methods in Linguistics
nodes.description: Fundamentals of scientific inquiry and methodology; basics of experimental design, statistical methods (descriptive, analytic, and exploratory) relevant to linguistics.

nodes.title: Predictive Modeling in Linguistics
nodes.description: Advanced methods in quantitative linguistics. Topics may include data exploration and visualization, classification trees, random forests, regression modeling, bootstrap methods, and Bayesian data analysis. Emphasis on building predictive models of linguistic data, with a focus on simulation, model comparison, and performance evaluation. Students complete statistical programming assignments and projects using real-world data.

nodes.title: Introduction to Phonetics
nodes.description: An introduction to the articulatory and acoustic properties of speech sounds. Survey of speech sounds found in the languages of the world. Emphasis on ear training and transcription using the International Phonetic Alphabet.

nodes.title: Introduction to Phonology
nodes.description: Introduction to the description and analysis of the sound patterns of natural language. Focus is on developing analytical skills for approaching data from a typologically diverse set of languages.

nodes.title: Introduction to Morphology
nodes.description: How meaning is encoded in words in the languages of the world. Morphological and morphophonemic processes, lexical categories, derivation and inflection, productivity, tense, aspect, mode, case, concord, valence changes (passives, antipassives, benefactives, causatives), morphological typologies.

nodes.title: Introduction to Syntax
nodes.description: Similarities and differences among languages in the grammatical devices they use to signal relations between words in phrases and sentences. Data from a range of languages is presented and analyzed.

nodes.title: Foundations of Computational Linguistics
nodes.prereq_text: Linguistics 102 or Computer Science 8 or equivalent experience.
nodes.description: An introduction to foundational ideas in computational linguistics, such as: n-gram language models; noisy channel models; supervised and unsupervised learning; and distributional semantics. Focus on developing an understanding of the intuitions behind the ideas, including relevant algorithms and math, and implementing this understanding in hands-on programming applications.

nodes.title: Advanced Computational Linguistics: Text Processing
nodes.description: Advanced topics in the computational processing of language in text form, such as: neural network language models; parsing; topic modeling; and machine translation. Focus on developing a high-level understanding of modern approaches and how to use them. Discussion of applications to areas such as natural language processing, corpus linguistics, and computational psycholinguistics.

nodes.title: Introduction to Semantics
nodes.description: Introduction to the study of meaning in language. Consideration of semantic fields, semantic components, semantic relations, categories, prototypes, frames, metaphor, pragmatics, indexicality, and speech acts.

nodes.title: Introduction to Historical Comparative Linguistics
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: E. Comparative and Historical Linguistics
nodes.description: An introduction to linguistic change, genetic classification of languages, and methods of reconstructing parent languages.

nodes.title: The Structure of Language and Sports
nodes.description: Examines the usage of language in organized sports, with analysis at lexical, morphological, syntactic, discursive, and phonological levels. Investigates how linguistic structure adapts to particular communicative contexts, such as media accounts and interactions among participants.

nodes.title: Regional Dialects and Varieties of English Around the World
nodes.description: Offers a comprehensive and in-depth survey of regional dialects of English throughout America and around the world. Examines dialect variation through both descriptive analysis as well as socio-historic accounts of the emergence of particular varieties.

nodes.title: Advanced Computational Linguistics: Speech Processing
nodes.description: Advanced topics in the computational processing of language in spoken form, such as: forced alignment; speech recognition; speaker recognition; and text-to-speech. Focus on developing a high-level understanding of modern approaches and how to use them. Discussion of applications to areas such as natural language processing, corpus linguistics, and computational psycholinguistics.

nodes.title: Corpus Linguistics
nodes.description: An introduction to computerized research methods which are applied to large databases of language used in natural communicative settings to supplement more traditional ways of linguistic analysis in all linguistic subdisciplines.

nodes.title: Discourse Analysis
nodes.prereq_text: Linguistics 20 or 109, or consent of instructor.
nodes.description: This course introduces students to the hands-on analysis of form and meaning in discourse, especially in naturally occurring conversation. Topics include referent accessibility, co-reference, and anaphora; resonance and coherence in dialogue; dialogue acts; constructions and information structure. Students learn to use basic computational tools for discourse analysis.

nodes.title: Neurolinguistics
nodes.description: An examination of how the brain supports language structure and language use, with an emphasis on how electrophysiological, neuroimaging, and lesion data contribute to linguistic theory and to our understanding of the mental representation of language.

nodes.title: Psychology of Language
nodes.description: An examination of the psychological foundations of language structure and use, including the cognitive processes involved in the comprehension, production, and recall of words, sentences, and discourse; first and second language acquisition; relationships among language, brain, cognition, and culture.

nodes.title: Sign Languages and Signing Communities
nodes.description: An introduction to the linguistics of sign languages and signing communities, including early and current perceptions of deaf people and sign languages. Covers the emergence of sign languages and signing communities as well as the linguistic structures, sociolinguistic contexts, and acquisition of sign languages.

nodes.title: Language as Culture
nodes.description: Views language through the lens of culture, exploring language as a sociocultural system that organizes meaning, memory, interpretation, authority, action, practice. How practices of speaking shape culture; intertextuality; linguistic and cultural relativity; relations between language, thought, and culture.

nodes.title: Sociocultural Linguistics
nodes.description: The study of language as a social phenomenon, with emphasis on language use outside the U.S. context. Quantitative and qualitative approaches to regional and social dialects, register, linguistic power and solidarity, language contact and change, multilingualism, codeswitching, language shift and loss.

nodes.title: Language, Gender, and Sexuality
nodes.description: The study of language as a resource for the production of gender and sexuality across cultures. Topics include: gender differentiation in language structure and use; intragender variation; language and discrimination; linguistic ideologies; language and identity.

nodes.title: Interdisciplinary Approaches to the Cultures, Languages, and Literatures of Latin America and Iberia
nodes.description: Issues pertinent to the diverse cultures, languages, and literatures of Latin America and Iberia. Disciplines and approaches may include: pre-Columbian studies, Spanish and Spanish American literatures, Portuguese and Brazilian literatures, translation studies, cultural, gender, and queer studies, romance language and linguistics.

nodes.title: North American Indigenous Languages
nodes.description: Survey of the several hundred native languages of North America, including the history of research on these languages, their classification, special structures, and their oral traditions.

nodes.title: Memes: Theory and Analysis of Cultural Evolution
nodes.description: This course examines the meme as the minimum unit of cultural evolution. Equal time is given to the theory of cultural evolution and hands-on analysis of memes. Focus on internet and pre-internet memes, including image-macro memes, videos, humor, proverbs, songs, games, words, technology, and other units of cultural evolution.

nodes.title: Introduction to First Language Acquisition
nodes.prereq_text: Linguistics 20 and Linguistics 106; concurrent enrollment accepted.
nodes.description: An introduction to the interdisciplinary enterprise of understanding first language acquisition, overview of different theoretical and methodological approaches, and introduction to developmental processes in sub-areas such as phonology, morphology, lexicon, syntax and semantics.

nodes.title: Introduction to Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages
nodes.description: Surveys theoretical and methodological issues related to teaching English as a second or foreign language. Students examine current research and pedagogy in TESOL and development in second language acquisition theory and evaluate teaching materials and develop classroom lessons.

nodes.title: English Grammar for Teachers
nodes.description: Covers English grammatical structures commonly the focus of teaching English as an additional language. Also considers key issues related to grammar in language teaching, such as error correction and deductive versus inductive methods of instruction.

nodes.title: Second Language Acquisition
nodes.description: An introduction to the theories and principles of how adults acquire a language other than their mother tongue, why it is more difficult than acquiring their first language, and what needs to be learned, from linguistic, psychological and social perspectives.

nodes.title: Phonological Typology
nodes.description: An introduction to the diversity of sound systems found in languages of the world. Considers the cross-linguistic distribution of phonological patterns and their treatment in phonological history.

nodes.title: Articulatory Phonetics
nodes.description: An introduction to the speech production system, with special focus on the articulatory structure of speech and the relation of this structure to the acoustic properties and perception of speech sounds. Considers the speech of populations with speech communication disorders, and presents an array of experimental techniques used to investigate speech.

nodes.title: Auditory Phonetics
nodes.description: Introduction to the auditory processing of speech, including the physiology of hearing, neurological processing of speech, perception of pitch, loudness, and temporal properties, frequency resolution, models of speech perception, and hearing disorders.

nodes.title: Topics in Clinical Linguistics
nodes.description: An introduction to clinical applications of linguistics relevant to speech-language pathology and audiology.

nodes.title: Introduction to Communication Sciences and Disorders
nodes.description: An intro to the field of communication sciences and disorders. This course will bridge lectures to clinical application with guided observation hours. Content may vary.

nodes.title: Language Disorders
nodes.description: Introduces a broad overview of the differential characteristics of language disorders and the principles of assessment and treatment.

nodes.title: Practicum in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages
nodes.description: Designed for students who are interested in teaching/tutoring English as a second or foreign language to adult learners, either abroad or in the United States. Through engagement with course curriculum/materials and through site-based observations, classroom and small group/individual teaching opportunities, and pedagogical feedback from a mentor teacher, practicum students will develop experiential knowledge regarding the applications of theoretical and pedagogical concepts in the teaching and learning of English as an additional language.

nodes.title: On-site Introductory Practicum
nodes.description: Designed for students who are interested in teaching/tutoring English as a second or foreign language to adult learners, either abroad or in the United States. Course content will vary.

nodes.title: Intercultural Communication
nodes.prereq_text: Any Linguistics or Communications course or consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Explores communication (verbal, nonverbal, mediated) between people from different cultural backgrounds. Topics include intersecting identities (national/regional, race/ethnicity, linguistic, gender, sexual orientation, etc.), intercultural relationships, cultural transitions, and intercultural conflict and dialogue. Integrates insights from social scientific, interpretive, and critical research.

nodes.title: Language Documentation
nodes.description: Issues in the creation of lasting multipurpose records of a language. Documentation as collaborative, community-based initiative. Description and documentation, archive creation, metadata, technologies, materials, ethics, ethnography, orthography, and multimedia. Students participate in a collaborative documentation project as primary coursework.

nodes.title: Professionalization in Speech-Language Pathology
nodes.prereq_text: Open to LING-SLSD majors and minors or by permission of instructor.

requires.text: Open to LING-SLSD majors and minors or by permission of instructor

nodes.description: Professional preparation for graduate studies and a career in speech-language pathology. Topics include identifying graduate/postbaccalaureate programs, résumé and dossier development, professional memberships and conferences.

nodes.title: Trans Linguistics
nodes.prereq_text: Must have taken one of the following courses: LING 130, 131, 132, 136, OR have consent of instructor.

items.text: Must have taken one of the following courses: LING 130

nodes.description: An exploration of language in relation to transgender, non-binary, and gender diverse communities and topics. Uses the tools of linguistics to consider pronouns and grammatical gender; inclusive language, linguistic justice, and language activism; gendered bodies and voices; language and transphobia; and trans representation in mediatized contexts.

nodes.title: The Structure of English
nodes.description: Introduction to the phonological, morphological, syntactic and discourse features of contemporary English.

nodes.title: Language in Social Interaction
nodes.description: What role does language play in social interaction? How do individuals use language to shape relationships with others within or across social groups? How do patterns of linguistic interaction constitute patterns of social organization? Emphasis on hands-on analysis of transcriptions and recordings of face-to-face interactions.

nodes.title: Language, Race, and Ethnicity
nodes.description: Linguistic practices of major ethnoracial groups in the United States, including African Americans, Asian Americans, European Americans, Latinxs, and Native Americans; examination of the linguistic effects of immigration and colonialism; bilingualism, translanguaging, language shift, and heritage language learning; linguistic interaction and contact between ethnoracial groups; language as a resource for ethnoracial identity; linguistic racism; linguistic activism.

nodes.title: Languages of the World
nodes.description: Introduction to the languages of the world: Geographical distribution; genetic (genealogical) classification, including comparison with genetics and archeology; structural properties and sociolinguistics of selected languages representing different parts of the world.

nodes.title: Language, Power and Learning
nodes.prereq_text: Departmental Approval Required to Finalize Registration.
nodes.description: Critical examination of institutional power related to education and linguistic and cultural diversity. Focus on Latinx communities; formal and informal learning; family practices; bilingual education; heritage languages; language and labor; language and racism; immigrant languages; racialized varieties of English.

nodes.title: Internship in Linguistics
nodes.description: Internship in a language-related work setting. Students apply concepts, methods, and issues from linguistics to professional contexts in education, business, government, nonprofit organizations and other fields.

nodes.title: Capstone Seminar
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division course in linguistics; consent of instructor.

items.text: completion of 2 upper-division course in linguistics

nodes.description: Original individual or collaborative research, creative, or action project in linguistics, typically taken in conjunction with LING 195 or equivalent. Weekly discussion of work in progress and professional preparation for graduate school in a workshop setting.

nodes.title: Group Studies in Linguistics
nodes.description: Limited to small groups whose interest and needs determine the central focus.

nodes.title: Honors Thesis
nodes.description: Guided research and writing of an original research paper to meet the requirements of the honors program in Linguistics.

nodes.description: Guided research and writing of an original research paper to meet the requirements of the honors program in Linguistics.

nodes.title: Independent Studies In Linguistics.
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in linguistics; consent of instructor.

items.text: completion of 2 upper-division courses in linguistics

nodes.description: Intended for the study of special areas within Linguistics.

nodes.title: Elementary Spanish I
nodes.description: Students will learn to use Spanish for communication in real, meaningful situations. This course will develop an understanding of basic grammatical concepts along with obtaining an appreciation of the various cultures of the Spanish-speaking world. The course follows a communicative approach and class time is primarily used for communication practice and Spanish will be spoken in class 99% of the time. By the end of this course students are expected to develop proficiency at the Novice-mid level.

nodes.title: Hybrid Elementary Spanish I
nodes.description: SPAN 1HY is the first course in a three-part hybrid Spanish series (SPAN 1HY, 2HY, 3HY), equivalent to the SPAN 1, 2, 3 Elementary Spanish sequence. Combining face-to-face instruction with online work, this course uses a communicative approach to develop basic Spanish skills for real-life situations. Class time focuses on active communication, with 99% of instruction conducted in Spanish. Students will build foundational grammar skills and gain insight into the diverse cultures of the Spanish-speaking world. By the end of the course, students are expected to reach Novice-Mid proficiency.

nodes.title: Elementary Spanish II
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 1 or Spanish W1 with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher.
nodes.description: Students will learn to use Spanish for communication in real, meaningful situations. This course will develop an understanding of basic grammatical concepts along with obtaining an appreciation of the various cultures of the Spanish-speaking world. The course follows a communicative approach and class time is primarily used for communication practice and Spanish will be spoken in class 99% of the time. By the end of this course students are expected to develop proficiency at the Novice-high level.

nodes.title: Hybrid Elementary Spanish II
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 1 or Spanish 1HY with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher.
nodes.description: SPAN 2HY is the second of the three Hybrid Elementary Spanish courses. Its hybrid format combines increased individual work with the online textbook, materials, and other web-based activities with reduced face-to-face class time and live guided conversation sessions. Course materials and activities focus on consolidating the same array of skills promoted in SPAN 2. Students learn to use Spanish for communication in real, meaningful situations, develop an understanding of basic grammatical concepts and an appreciation of the various cultures of the Spanish-speaking world.

nodes.title: Elementary Spanish III
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 2 or Spanish W2 with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher.
nodes.description: Students will learn to use Spanish for communication in real, meaningful situations. This course will develop an understanding of basic grammatical concepts along with obtaining an appreciation of various cultures of the Spanish-speaking world. The course follows a communicative approach and class time is primarily used for communication practice; Spanish will be spoken in class 99% of the time. By the end of this course students are expected to develop proficiency at the Novice-high or Intermediate-low level.

nodes.title: Hybrid Elementary Spanish III
nodes.prereq_text: Completion of Spanish 2 or Spanish 2HY with a grade of P, or a grade of C or higher.
nodes.description: SPAN 3HY is the third of the three Hybrid Elementary Spanish courses. Its hybrid format combines increased individual work with the online textbook, materials, and other web-based activities with reduced face-to-face class time and live guided conversation sessions. Course materials and activities focus on consolidating the same array of skills promoted in SPAN 3. Students learn to use Spanish for communication in real, meaningful situations, develop an understanding of basic grammatical concepts and an appreciation of the various cultures of the Spanish-speaking world.

nodes.title: Intermediate Spanish I
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 3, Spanish 3SS, 3HY, with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher; or a score of 3 on the AP Spanish Language Examination; or a score of 3 on the AP Spanish Language & Culture Examination.
nodes.description: Begins review of basic grammar and syntax.

nodes.title: Intermediate Spanish II
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 4 with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher; or a score of 4 on the AP Spanish Language Examination; or a score of 4 on the AP Spanish Language and Culture Examination; or a score of 3 on the AP Spanish Literature and Culture Examination.
nodes.description: Continues the review of basic grammar and syntax. Course conducted in Spanish.

nodes.title: Intermediate Spanish III
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 5 with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher; or a score of 5 on the AP Spanish Language Examination; or a score of 5 on the AP Spanish Language and Culture Examination; or a score of 3 on the AP Spanish Literature Examination; or a score of 4 on the AP Spanish Literature and Culture Examination.
nodes.description: An intensive course designed to develop students' skills in reading, oral, and written expression by reading and discussing Hispanic texts, and writing compositions on related topics.

nodes.title: Intermediate Spanish for Heritage Speakers
nodes.prereq_text: Instructor or department approval required to finalize enrollment.
nodes.description: SPAN 15 is designed for students who learned Spanish at home or as a first language and provides them with the language and learning skills required to successfully complete more advanced Spanish courses (SPAN 16A/B). It focuses on formal Spanish, grammar, and reading with an emphasis on writing and vocabulary building. Students will develop awareness of linguistic registers, and practice formal speaking and writing skills through readings and discussions based on Hispanic topics in the United States and other Spanish-speaking countries. Special attention will be paid to those aspects that Spanish speakers in the United States find most problematic.

nodes.title: Spanish for Heritage Speakers
nodes.description: Addresses on a university level the needs and strengths of students with Spanish speaking background but no formal language training in Spanish speaking countries. Emphasizes skill in composition, advanced reading comprehension, standard versus vernacular usages, cross language interference, etc.

nodes.title: Spanish for Heritage Speakers
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 16A with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher.
nodes.description: Addresses on university level the needs and strengths of students with Spanish speaking background but no formal language training in Spanish speaking countries. Emphasizes more complex skills in composition and advanced reading comprehension than Spanish 16A, as well as standard versus vernacular usages, cross language interferences, etc.

nodes.title: Advanced Grammar and Composition
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 6 with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher; or a score of 4 or 5 on the AP Spanish Literature Examination; or a score of 5 on the AP Spanish Literature and Culture Examination.
nodes.description: Intensive course taught in Spanish designed to reinforce students' comprehension and ability to express themselves in Spanish, both orally and in writing, and to develop the students' vocabularies and awareness of syntactical structures in the language.

nodes.title: Introduction to Hispanic Linguistics
nodes.prereq_text: SPAN 16B or SPAN 25 (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Introduction to linguistic theories, methods, and problems as applied to Spanish. Taught in Spanish with Spanish examples.

nodes.title: Advanced Composition through Literature
nodes.description: The study of the finer points of Spanish grammar and syntax. Stress is placed on writing critical analyses of literary readings.

nodes.title: Advanced Composition through Literature
nodes.description: The study of the finer points of Spanish grammar and syntax. Stress is placed on writing critical analyses of literary readings.

nodes.title: Introduction to Hispanic Studies
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 16B or Spanish 25 or consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Introduces students to key concepts, methods, and debates in Hispanic Studies, with a focus on literature, media, cultural production, and historical contexts from Spain, Latin America, and U.S. Latinx communities. Students learn to analyze texts and cultural artifacts using interdisciplinary approaches, including cultural studies, history, and critical theory. The course provides a foundation for upper-division coursework and strengthens analytical, writing, and research skills in Spanish. Taught in Spanish.

nodes.title: Beyond Advanced Spanish Proficiency
nodes.description: Designed to provide students who have completed Span 25 or Span 16B and one additional upper-division Spanish course with the opportunity to practice the four language skills: speaking, listening, reading, and writing. Students will practice different communicative skills, from defending an opinion to mastering transactions and exchanges.

nodes.title: Teaching Spanish for Heritage Speakers
nodes.description: Designed for students who have completed Span 100 and who are considering a teaching career. The course covers frequent issues encountered when working with students who have learned Spanish through their family history or place of origin.

nodes.title: Introduction to Latin American and Iberian Studies
nodes.description: Designed to acquaint students with current research on the main areas of Latin American and Iberian Studies.

nodes.title: Introduction to Latin American and Iberian Studies - Honors Section
nodes.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in SPAN 106 or LAIS 100; honors standing in LAIS or the College of Letters and Science.
nodes.description: Eligible students are invited to enroll in the honors seminar, which is generally taught by the course instructor.

nodes.title: Interdisciplinary Approaches to the History and Societies of Latin America and Iberia
nodes.description: Issues central to the study of Latin America and Iberia across the social sciences and history. Topics include nationalism, revolution, politics and the state, economic development and international relations, labor, popular culture, race, gender, religion, migration, environment, imperialism, and colonialism.

nodes.title: Interdisciplinary Approaches to the Cultures, Languages, and Literatures of Latin America and Iberia
nodes.description: Issues pertinent to the diverse cultures, languages, and literatures of Latin America and Iberia. Disciplines and approaches may include: pre-Columbian studies, Spanish and Spanish American literatures, Portuguese and Brazilian literatures, translation studies, cultural, gender, and queer studies, romance language and linguistics.

nodes.title: Spanish in the United States: The Language and Its Speakers
nodes.description: Study of Spanish used in United States by native and immigrant groups: Mexicans, Chicanos, Cubans, Puerto Ricans and others in Spanish-speaking enclaves. Focus on language and social and cultural manifestations arising in contact between linguistically different groups. Taught in Spanish.

nodes.title: Spanish Literature from the Beginning to the Present
nodes.description: Medieval Spanish literature.

nodes.title: Spanish Literature from the Beginning to the Present
nodes.description: Golden age literature.

nodes.title: Spanish Literature from the Beginning to the Present
nodes.description: Eighteenth- and nineteenth-century Spanish literature.

nodes.title: Spanish Literature from the Beginning to the Present
nodes.description: Twentieth-century Spanish literature.

nodes.title: Spanish-American Literature from the Beginning to the Present
nodes.description: Colonial Spanish-American literature.

nodes.title: Spanish-American Literature from the Beginning to the Present
nodes.description: Twentieth-century Spanish-American literature.

nodes.title: Non-Castilian Literatures of Spain
nodes.description: Introduction to Spains medieval linguistic and cultural diversity through literary works written in such languages as Latin, Arabic, Hebrew, Mozarabic, Occitan, Catalan-Valencian, Galician-Portuguese and Galician. Texts read in Spanish or English translation.

nodes.title: Non-Castilian Literatures of Spain
nodes.description: Introduction to Spains linguistic and cultural diversity in modern and contemporary times through literary works written in Asturian, Basque, Catalan and Galician. Texts read in Spanish translation.

nodes.title: Introduction to Translation I
nodes.description: Comprises topics necessary to develop skills that are needed for writing at a specialized level and to carry out written translation into and from Spanish, mostly texts on business and medical topics.

nodes.title: Specialized Translation - Legal
nodes.description: Comprised of topics necessary in developing skills for writing at a specialized level, and with specialized vocabulary, for the legal profession.

nodes.title: Specialized Translation - Technical
nodes.description: Comprised of topics necessary in developing skills for writing at a specialized level, and with specialized vocabulary and format, for the translation of different types of technical texts (instruction manuals, medical, patents, etc.).

nodes.title: Spanish Institutions and Culture
nodes.description: Study of the development of the Spanish nation, with special focus on key social and political institutions, the arts and major currents of thought.

nodes.title: Psycholinguistics
nodes.description: An introduction to core areas of Spanish psycholinguistics: speech perception, word recognition, language comprehension, language production, first language acquisition, bilingualism, language disorders and aphasiology. Goals: 1)to introduce students to the key findings and central debates within psycholinguistic research; 2)to introduce students to the tools and methods of psycholinguistic research; 3)to introduce students to research practice; 4)to manage effective interaction within the intercultural context. Students will develop an experiment design, and collect/analyze data. Depending on their performance, students will be invited to work and/or volunteer at the Bilingualism, Translation, & Cognition Laboratory.

nodes.title: Psycholinguistics
nodes.description: An introduction to core areas of Spanish psycholinguistics: speech perception, word recognition, language comprehension, language production, first language acquisition, bilingualism, language disorders & aphasiology. Goals: 1)to introduce students to the key findings & central debates within psycholinguistic research; 2)to introduce students to the tools and methods of psycholinguistic research; 3)to introduce students to research practice; 4)to manage effective interaction within the intercultural context. Students will develop an experiment design, and collect/analyze data. Depending on their performance, students will be invited to work and/or volunteer at the Bilingualism, Translation, & Cognition Laboratory. Taught in English.

nodes.title: Spanish Cinema
nodes.description: Introduces twentieth-century Spain through significant films, analyzing how cinema represents social, political, and cultural issues, as well as key themes, genres, and filmmakers.

nodes.title: Spanish Cinema
nodes.description: Introduces twentieth-century Spain through significant films, analyzing how cinema represents social, political, and cultural issues, as well as key themes, genres, and filmmakers. Taught in English.

nodes.title: Gastronomy of the Americas through Literature
nodes.description: An in-depth look at the gastronomy of specific geographical and cultural regions of Latin America through a selection of literary texts and films. From Pre-Columbian to current gastronomical influences from around the world, students will learn about ancient grains, protein alternatives, non-wheat carbohydrates, common herbs and spices in connection with the region in which native people grow, preserve and consume them. Other cultural and culinary influences that have shaped the gastronomy of Latin American today will be emphasized to highlight the fusion and a culinary syncretism observed within the rich and diverse Latin American cuisine. A culinary selection of traditional dishes will be prepared.

nodes.title: Gastronomy of the Americas through Literature
nodes.description: An in-depth look at the gastronomy of specific geographical and cultural regions of Latin America through a selection of literary texts and films. From Pre-Columbian to current gastronomical influences from around the world, students will learn about ancient grains, protein alternatives, non-wheat carbohydrates, common herbs and spices in connection with the region in which native people grow, preserve and consume them. Other cultural and culinary influences that have shaped the gastronomy of Latin American today will be emphasized to highlight the fusion and a culinary syncretism observed within the rich and diverse Latin American cuisine. A culinary selection of traditional dishes will be prepared. Taught in English.

nodes.title: Creative Writing
nodes.description: Designed primarily for students who are inclined to write fictional prose and/or poetry in Spanish.

nodes.title: The Fantastic and Its Development in Spanish-American Short Story
nodes.description: Exploration of the multiple manifestations of the Fantastic in Spanish American short story from its origin, linked to nineteenth-century sensationalistic journalism, up to neofantastic mode appearing circa 1950, with its more epistemological goals.

nodes.title: Spanish Golden Age Poetry I
nodes.description: Lyric poetry of the sixteenth century: Garcilaso, Luis de Leon, San Juan de La Cruz, and others.

nodes.title: The Spanish Civil War: Conflict, Culture, and Memory
nodes.description: An introduction to the Spanish Civil War (1936-1939), an event that had a tremendous impact over Spains twentieth-century history, culture, and society. Through the study of distinct number of cultural products (memoirs, novels, films, photographs), we cover the social and cultural history of the war, the way it has been represented in different periods of history, as well as why and how it has been the inspiration of many works of art (Picasso), films (Del Toro) and literary pieces (Max Aub) produced all over the world.

nodes.title: The Spanish Civil War: Conflict, Culture, and Memory
nodes.description: An introduction to the Spanish Civil War (1936-1939), an event that had a tremendous impact over Spains twentieth-century history, culture, and society. Through the study of distinct number of cultural products (memoirs, novels, films, photographs), we cover the social and cultural history of the war, the way it has been represented in different periods of history, as well as why and how it has been the inspiration of many works of art (Picasso), films (Del Toro) and literary pieces (Max Aub) produced all over the world.Taught in English.

nodes.title: Spanish Laughter: The Politics of Humor in Spain
nodes.description: This course presents a historical account of humor in Spain, and the evolution of its political value. Through the analysis of a wide range of cultural artifacts such as short stories, tv shows, films, comic books, and paintings, we will analyze the changing role that humor has played in the Spanish public sphere from the early modern period to the present day, as well as how it has been an important tool that Spaniards have taken advantage of to address different social fears and challenges.

nodes.title: Spanish Laughter: The Politics of Humor in Spain

Through the analysis of a wide range of cultural artifacts such as short stories, tv shows, films, comic books, and paintings, we will analyze the changing role that humor has played in the Spanish public sphere from the early modern period to the present day, as well as how it has been an important tool that Spaniards have taken advantage of to address different social fears and challenges. Taught in English.

nodes.title: Spain at the Crossroads: Tradition and Modernity
nodes.description: Selected topics related to the study of the major literary movements and currents of thought in Spanish Literature during the 18th and 19th centuries, such as Enlightenment, "Costumbrismo", Nationalism, Romanticism, Realism, or Naturalism. Analysis of the major poets, playwrights, and novelists of the period. Readings and discussions in Spanish.

nodes.title: Modern Mexican Literature
nodes.description: Study of texts explaining the development of Mexican culture and literature. Topic and writers: modernism (from Gutierrez Najera to Tablada); the novel of the Mexican revolution (Azuela); and the modern essay (Alfonso Reyes and Octavio Paz).

nodes.title: Golden Age Drama
nodes.description: The classic comedia, by Lope, Tirso, Alarcon, Calderon, and other dramatists.

nodes.title: Golden Age Drama
nodes.description: The classic comedia, by Lope, Tirso, Alarcon, Calderon, and other dramatists.

nodes.title: Contemporary Mexican Literature
nodes.description: Continued study of major trends in Mexican literature as evidenced in selected works of the following authors: the poetry of Lopez Velarde and Octavio Paz; the contemporaneos (Torres Bodet, Villaurrutia, Pellicer); and contemporary fiction (Yanez, Rulfo, Arreola, and Fuentes).

nodes.title: U.S. Latino Literature
nodes.description: A comparative study of the literature and culture of the diverse Latino populations of the United States, including Chicano, Puerto Rican, Cuban-American, Dominican-American, and other U.S. Latino groups. Writers, genres, and periods vary from quarter to quarter, emphasizing salient examples of fiction, poetry, drama, the essay, film or art. Taught in English.

nodes.title: Cervantes: Don Quijote
nodes.description: Reading and discussion of the first and second parts of Don Quixote.

nodes.title: Don Quixote (in English Translation)
nodes.description: Reading, examination, and discussion (all in English) of the first part of Cervantes' masterpiece and its reflections on world literature.

nodes.title: Spanish for Healthcare
nodes.description: Designed for students interested in expanding and applying their knowledge of Spanish to the medical field. Students will learn and apply targeted vocabulary/grammar and develop bicultural/bilingual competency of healthcare issues in Hispanic countries and the US.

nodes.title: Narratives of Identity: Art, Culture and Politics in Spain
nodes.description: Focusing on a wide range of its cultural manifestations (Art, Architecture, Cinema, Literature, Language, Gastronomy), this course offers an interdisciplinary approach, conceiving Spain as a multilayered space that is furnished by Roman, French, and Muslim legacies and that drove the shaping of a singular culture.

nodes.title: Business Spanish
nodes.description: Real-life situations in the workplace will present students with the appropriate vocabulary for business environments. Students learn to write formal documents, how to express themselves orally, and to assess the business environment of different Spanish-speaking countries from a cultural perspective.

nodes.title: Filmmakers Series
nodes.description: A focus on some of the most important filmmakers from the Hispanic World (Buuel, Almodvar, Saura, Reygadas). The course follows the development of their careers, analyzing the main topics and contexts

nodes.title: Almodvar's Spain: Cinema and Society
nodes.description: This course focuses on analyzing Pedro Almodvar's work in relation to its historical and social context. We will examine some of his most notable films and observe the evolution of his cinematic style. Additionally, we will explore how his films tackle social conflicts that have impacted Spanish society from the end of the Franco dictatorship to the present.

nodes.title: Soccer: The Cultural Impact of a Global Game
nodes.description: Soccer is a mirror of our world and an expression of our greatest tragedies and hopes.Thiscourse seeks to use soccer as a tool for learning about politics, economics, culture, society, philosophy, art, literature andthe human condition in the Hispanic world.

nodes.title: Barcelona: The Making of an Urban Landscape
nodes.description: Explores the rich history and cultural evolution of Barcelona, one of the most iconic cities in the world. From its humble beginnings as a Roman colony to its current status as a bustling cosmopolitan city, Barcelona has undergone numerous transformations throughout its history. Through a multidisciplinary approach, which includes a combination of films, readings, and other visual materials, we delve into the construction of Barcelona as a modern metropolis and trace the ways in which its cultural legacies are still present in its urban landscape today.

nodes.title: Basque Studies
nodes.description: An overview of the cultural and historical characteristics of the Basque Country while analyzing how minoritized groups, such as the Basque, negotiate their identity in the face of globalization.

nodes.title: Basque Studies
nodes.description: An overview of the cultural and historical characteristics of the Basque Country while analyzing how minoritized groups, such as the Basque, negotiate their identity in the face of globalization. Taught in English.

nodes.title: Basque Language and Culture
nodes.description: An intensive course for students with no previous study of the Basque language.

nodes.title: Basque Language and Culture
nodes.description: Continues activities commenced in Spanish 154A.

nodes.title: Basque Language and Culture
nodes.description: Continues activities commenced in SPAN 154A and SPAN 154B.

nodes.title: Discourses of Love and Desire: from The Book of Good Love to the Present
nodes.description: This course sequence (SPAN 155 A - B) traces the literary constructions, elaborations, and treatments of love in Spanish literature from Middle Ages to the present. SPAN 155A (Pre-1700) focuses specifically on the development of courtly love and neoplatonic visions of love in the Iberian Peninsula as they pertain to a variety of literary and cultural forms.

nodes.title: Discourses of Love and Desire: from The Book of Good Love to the Present
nodes.description: This course sequence (SPAN 155 A - B) traces the literary constructions, elaborations, and treatments of love in Spanish literature from Middle Ages to the present. SPAN 155B (Post- 1700) explores the psychological and sociological implications and the cultural significance of love in a variety of art forms, poetry, drama, novel and film.

nodes.title: Introduction to Galician Studies
nodes.description: The uniqueness of the culture and language of Galicia, its history, ethnography, folklore, and literature, in Galician and Spanish.

nodes.title: Exploring Minor Theatrical Genres: Analysis, Writing, and Staging
nodes.description: Familiarizes students with a usually understudied field, the "minor" genres of drama during the Golden Age. Combines theory with praxis by asking the students to write and stage their own "minor" texts as a final project for the class. Performances are open to the general public.

nodes.title: Survey of Transborder Cultural Production
nodes.description: A general overview of the literature, music, and visual arts created by Transborder cultural producers in the U.S. / México border region. People's socio-historical experiences are examined to understand ethnicity, creativity, and world citizenship.

nodes.title: Literature and Technology in Latin-America
nodes.description: Explores how Latin America theoretical discourses have reflected upon technology, including vaccines, agriculture, film and contemporary cyberpunk fiction.

nodes.title: Horror and Mystery
nodes.description: A panoramic view of short stories and films belonging to the horror genre in Spain and Latin America. The course offers contextualization and analysis of each story or film. Included are short stories by Espronceda, Bcquer, Ochoa, Zorrilla, Quiroga, Cortzar, Anderson Imbert and films by Gonzlez, Larraaga, Ibez Serrador, Naschy, Franco, Padrn and Brugus.

nodes.title: Nicaraguan Poetry
nodes.description: Surveys the poetry of Nicaragua from its origins to the present. It frames key authors and representative poetic texts within their literary and cultural context. Poets include Daro, Corts, Selva, Cuadra, and Belli.

nodes.title: Andean Literature, Music, and Culture
nodes.description: This course focuses on literature, music and culture of certain ethnic groups inhabiting the Andean region of South America including, but not limited to, the Aymara and Quechua peoples, their cosmovision and their languages. Through literary texts belonging to different genres, and through films, special attention is placed on expressions of syncretism in seasonal festivals in which pre-Hispanic, European, and African music traditions and religions were shaped due to forced migration, wars and colonization. A strong emphasis on the ecological regions of the nations that share the Andean mountain range contextualizes current indigenous movements of resistance against the degradation of its environment and the impact on its culture.

nodes.title: The Universe in a Nutshell: J.L. Borges and his Fictions
nodes.description: A study of one of the greatest writers of the twentieth century: Jorge Luis Borges. Explores his various creative registers, from his short stories in the vein of fantastic literature, to his poetry and his work as an essayist. The perspective of the course is comparative around topics (some seminal, some relatively unexplored) that Borges treats across a variety of literary genres.

nodes.title: The Universe in a Nutshell: J.L. Borges and his Fictions
nodes.description: A study of one of the greatest writers of the twentieth century: Jorge Luis Borges. Explores his various creative registers, from his short stories in the vein of fantastic literature, to his poetry and his work as an essayist. The perspective of the course is comparative around topics (some seminal, some relatively unexplored) that Borges treats across a variety of literary genres. Taught in English.

nodes.title: Posmodernismo
nodes.description: Study of the Spanish and Spanish-American Postmodernistas, exploring the link between the culture of modernity and the emergence of a colloquial, prosaic, but lyrical discourse in late nineteenth and twentieth century Spanish and Spanish-American poetry.

nodes.title: Literature and Cultural Identity in the Spanish Caribbean
nodes.description: Survey of Spanish Caribbean literature from the standpoint of interaction of culture and race. It traces the counterpoint among the diverse ethnic groups that populate the Caribbean and the manner in which the discourse ofthe oppressor and the oppressed intertwine.

nodes.title: Spain's "Disaster" and the Avant-Garde
nodes.description: Focuses on Spain’s political and cultural transformation from the world’s largest empire to an isolated country. The course covers the contentious discussions about the modernization of the country and the irruption of the Avant-Garde

nodes.title: Latin America on Film
nodes.description: An exploration of Latin American film and how this medium represents the cultures, histories and politics of the region. We will study a selection of films encompassing different genres, styles and historical periods, including some key works by influential Latin American filmmakers.

nodes.title: Lorca, Tradition, Modernity, and the Avant Garde
nodes.description: A study of Lorcas poetry and theater in the context of the major artistic, sociopolitical and historical transformations of the early 20th century, exploring how traditional Spanish culture and avant-garde innovation intersect each other in his work.

nodes.title: The Hispanic Novel and Cinema
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 102L OR Spanish 30 (Prerequisite may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Study of three or four Hispanic novels vis-a-vis their film versions, permitting analysis of narrative in both genres, using existing films and videos based on masterpieces of Hispanic literature. Taught in Spanish.

nodes.title: Contemporary Spanish Cultural Studies
nodes.description: An interdisciplinary approach to the understanding of present-day Spain, focusing on popular music, TV and literature from the 1960s until today.

nodes.title: Spanish-American Thought
nodes.description: Leading social, institutional, intellectual, and artistic trends from the sixteenth century to the present.

nodes.title: Mexican Culture
nodes.description: Social, institutional, intellectual, and artistic trends in the developmentof modern Mexico.

nodes.title: Chicana/o Novels
nodes.description: Reading, analysis and critique of the contemporary Chicano novel as it pertains to the Chicano experience.

nodes.title: Special Topics in Peninsular Literature and Culture
nodes.description: Special topics in Peninsular literature and culture.

nodes.title: Hispanic Poetry: 1900 to 1945
nodes.description: Reading and discussion of twentieth-century Spanish and Spanish-American poets and trends in their socio-historical context.

nodes.title: Special Topics in Latin American Literature and Culture
nodes.description: Special topics in Latin American literature and culture.

nodes.title: Science Fiction in Latin America
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 30 or Spanish 102L (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: An exploration of science fiction narrative and film from Latin America. Through a selection of works by Latin American authors from the early 20th century until the present, we will study how the history, cultures, and traditions of the region have shaped the genre of science fiction, and how this affords a singular perspective to think about topics like technology, neoliberalism, ethnicity, colonialism, the environment, and the future of the planet.

nodes.title: Gender in Basque Culture
nodes.description: Using Basque culture as a case study, this course explores how gender intersects with other crucial issues such as ethnicity, nationhood, and globalization.

nodes.title: Conflict, Memory, and Cultural Production
nodes.description: Explores how cultural artifacts like novels and films articulate individual and collective histories of violence.

nodes.title: Basque Studies through Literature and Culture in Translation (Spanish/English)
nodes.description: Delves deeper into the diversity of topics that make up Basque Studies, and analyses historical, but also contemporary socio-cultural topics related to the Basque country and the Basque diaspora abroad. Can be taken either as a continuation of SPAN 153E or a self-standing course on Basque Studies, where literary and cultural materials are presented in their English, Spanish, and possibly also French translations depending on student interest and language choice.

nodes.title: Basque Film
nodes.description: Provides a critical examination of the history and poetics of Basque film from the 20th century to the present.

nodes.title: Contemporary Spanish-American Short Story
nodes.description: A study of the trends, themes and techniques of the contemporary Spanish American short story with emphasis on major authors such as Borges, Cortzar, Ocampo, Onetti, Rulfo, Carpentier, Garca Mrquez, and others.

nodes.title: The Spanish-American Nueva Novela
nodes.description: Readings of such authors as Borges, Rulfo Fuentes, Vargas Llosa, Garcia Marquez, Donoso. Emphasis put on the innovative structure and language brought to Hispanic literature by the so-called Nueva Novela.

nodes.title: Selected Topics in Hispanic Linguistics
nodes.description: Topics for the course reflect the research interests of faculty members.

nodes.title: Teaching Spanish
nodes.description: An introduction to the field of Second Language Acquisition and Foreign Language Teaching. Special attention will be given to topics that have proved most problematic for native speakers of English who learn Spanish as a second language. After a general overview of Applied Linguistics, the course will cover topics dealing with teaching situations. This course is a theoretical and practical review of how to teach writing, reading, communicative competence, listening comprehension and culture at all levels of Spanish study.

nodes.title: Translation, Technology, and the Mind: An Introduction to Translation and Cognition
nodes.description: Translation, Technology, and the Mind is an introduction to technology in translation and interpretation. Students will learn about translation and interpretation, technologies used in the field and in research, and how translation/interpretation is performed in the mind. Throughout the course, students will have the opportunity to reflect on their own uses of technology as they develop their translation and interpretation skills.

nodes.title: Modern Hispanic Drama
nodes.description: Representative dramatists of Spain such as Unamuno, Valle-Inclan, Garcia Lorca, Buero Vallejo, and others.

nodes.title: Modernismo
nodes.description: Introduction to the poetry and prose of Hispanic Modernismo. Major writers and their most representative works: Marti, Dario, Rodo, Lugones. Lyric poetry, short story, novel, the essay, and other forms are studied.

nodes.title: Borges and His Precursors
nodes.description: This course focuses on Borges the Reader, and traces in particular his affinities with North American and European literatures.

nodes.title: Capstone Seminar - Peninsular Spanish Studies
nodes.description: The Capstone Seminar offers outstanding Spanish Majors the opportunity to conduct research alongside M.A. and Ph.D. students in the Department of Spanish and Portuguese. The course aims to improve the students' critical thinking and ability to analyze and contextualize primary and secondary sources within Peninsular Spanish Literature. Students learn to identify and locate reliable sources, compile and present bibliographical data in a consistent format, and improve their ability to write scholarly prose in clear, idiomatic Spanish.

nodes.title: Capstone Seminar - Latin American Studies
nodes.description: The Capstone Seminar offers outstanding Spanish Majors the opportunity to conduct research alongside M.A. and Ph.D. students in the Department of Spanish and Portuguese. The course aims to improve the students' critical thinking and ability to analyze and contextualize primary and secondary sources within Latin American Literature. Students learn to identify and locate reliable sources, compile and present bibliographical data in a consistent format, and improve their ability to write scholarly prose in clear, idiomatic Spanish.

nodes.title: Spanish American Women's Writing
nodes.description: An introduction to nineteenth- and twentieth-century Spanish American women's writings. Themes may include women's participation in the formation of national literatures, their engagement with a tradition of women's writing, and issues of authorship and authority.

nodes.title: Senior Honors Independent Research
nodes.description: The student will engage in research lead ing to a paper of considerable depth and complexity on a topic dealing with the literature and/or languageof Spain and Spanish America.

nodes.title: Independent Studies in Spanish
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of two upper-division courses in Spanish and consent of department.

items.text: completion of two upper-division courses in Spanish

nodes.description: Independent studies in selected subjects not covered by course offerings.

nodes.title: Online Elementary Spanish I
nodes.description: Span W1 is the first course of the Elementary Spanish three course sequence delivered in a fully online format. By the end of this course students are expected to develop basic proficiency in Spanish at the Novice-mid level.

nodes.title: Online Elementary Spanish II
nodes.prereq_text: Spanish 1 with a grade of P or a grade of C or higher.
nodes.description: SPAN W 2 is the second of the three Elementary Spanish courses offered in a fully online format. Its online format combines technology-based language instruction with online class meetings and live guided conversation sessions. Course materials and activities focus on consolidating the same array of skills promoted in the regular Elementary Span II course. Students learn to use Spanish for communication in real, meaningful situations, develop an understanding of basic grammatical concepts and an appreciation of the various cultures of the Spanish-speaking world. Each week, students attend one online class session and one conversation session. There is individual work with the textbook, online materials, and other web-based activities.
